appliesWhen: The running Node is a different build from the snapshot's nodeVersion — i.e. the scheduled nightly/RC jobs only. The per-PR snapshot-check job installs the pinned version and ignores this file entirely, exemptions included.
scope: Only the exact flags named here are excused, and only in the listed direction. A `changed` entry excuses only its exact `from` -> `to` shapes. Any other added, removed or changed flag still fails the job loudly.
whyNotJustRefreshTheSnapshot: snapshot-check feeds snapshot.nodeVersion straight into setup-node, so absorbing a nightly's flag set would re-pin that deterministic gate to a nightly build. The snapshot stays pinned to a released Node; pre-release deltas live here until they ship.

--experimental-strip-private-modules.why: New experimental flag on the dev line (nodejs/node#63869): lets Node's own type stripping run on TypeScript inside node_modules for packages marked private. Off by default, and crates/nub-core/src/node/feature_matrix.rs carries no band for it, so nub never injects it.
--experimental-strip-private-modules.removeWhen: The snapshot moves to a released Node that carries the flag; the snapshot then records it directly and this entry is inert.

--experimental-repl-await.why: Node made the flag an accepted no-op once the REPL moved onto the inspector, where top-level await is always on (nodejs/node#64986). It still parses, and feature_matrix.rs never injects it.
--experimental-repl-await.removeWhen: The snapshot moves to a released Node where the flag is a no-op.

--experimental-websocket.why: Node dropped the --no-experimental-websocket opt-out and left the flag as an accepted no-op (nodejs/node#65284). feature_matrix.rs injects it only on [20.10.0, 22.0.0), never on this Node, and the no-op still parses.
--experimental-websocket.removeWhen: The snapshot moves to a released Node where the flag is a no-op.
